items.title: Kurva Patah
items.summary:
Intercepted elliptic curve Diffie-Hellman parameters were recovered. Can you break the discrete logarithm on this flawed curve and decrypt the secret transmission?
TL;DR Kurva Patah is a cryptography challenge featuring a vulnerable Elliptic Curve Diffie-Hellman (ECDH) implementation. Because the curve’s group order is exceptionally small (n=10092n = 10092n=10092), the Elliptic Curve Discrete Logarithm Problem (ECDLP) is trivial to solve via direct point multiplication brute force. Once the target’s private key ddd is recovered, the AES-128-CBC key is derived from SHA-256(str(d))[:16]\text{SHA-256}(\text{str}(d))[:16]SHA-256(str(d))[:16], decrypting the flag ciphertext. items.title: Sandi Berlapis
items.summary:
A multi-layered cryptographic pipeline was used to obscure a confidential message. Can you reverse the transformations in the exact inverse order to recover the flag?
TL;DR Sandi Berlapis is a cryptography challenge featuring a four-stage sequential encoding pipeline: XOR with a repeating key (PH4NT0M), byte reversal, Base64 encoding, and Hex encoding. Because all four transformations are deterministic and completely reversible, inverting the operations in reverse order (Hex Decode →\rightarrow→ Base64 Decode →\rightarrow→ Byte Reversal →\rightarrow→ XOR) recovers the original flag. Encoder Mechanism Analysis The challenge provides the encryption script encoder.py:
